title: unified-rollouts-probing-staged-shadow-autorollback-workflow-improvements
author: Carla Nguyen
release_notes: Enhances probing stage for staged shadow canary workflows: tighter quorum logic, improved telemetry for rollback decisions, and additional e2e stability tests.
body: Summary: This PR refines the probing/staged shadow canary autorollback workflow to reduce false positives during warm-up probes and improve observability for multi-metric rollback decisions. Motivation: We observed spurious rollbacks during high-variance workloads where short-lived probe failures triggered full rollbacks. This change introduces a quorum-based probe aggregation, adds a short stabilization window before counting probes toward the quorum during initial warm-up, and surfaces more granular telemetry to the rollback decision engine and dashboards. What changed: 1) Quorum aggregation: probes now vote using a sliding window and require a configurable quorum percentage over N probes before triggering quarantine or rollback; 2) Warm-up stabilization: the first M probes after rollout or probe-stage changes are treated as provisional and do not count toward quorum until a stabilization timer elapses; 3) Metric matching improvements: composite-metric support added so policy can require multiple metrics (latency P95, error rate, and model output regression) to cross thresholds concurrently; 4) Observability: new per-probe traces and per-stage histograms plus tagging for shadow vs. production traffic, exported to tracing and metric backends; 5) e2e and integration tests covering corner cases where probe variance is high; 6) Backwards-compatible default config preserves existing behavior unless policies opt into the new quorum/stabilization fields. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-5324) - [x] Unit tests for quorum and warm-up logic - [x] e2e tests for staged shadow probing under synthetic variance - [x] Observability dashboards updated - [x] Rollout plan documented in PR - [x] No breaking changes to existing rollout policies Migration/compatibility: New fields are optional: quorum_percentage, quorum_window, warmup_provisional_count, stabilization_seconds, and composite_metric_rules. Existing rollout configs will behave exactly as before. Testing: Added unit tests for the autorollback engine and probing aggregator, integration tests against the rollout simulator, and an e2e suite that runs a staged shadow canary with injected variance to validate no rollback until quorum/stabilization conditions are met. Observability: Metrics emitted: rollout.probe.count, rollout.probe.votes, rollout.probe.quorum_hit, rollout.probe.stabilized, rollout.rollback.decision_reasons (labelled by metric). Traces: probe-span includes payload hashes and shadow tag. Rollout plan: staged rollout to canary environments for 48 hours with feature flag rollout.enable_probing_quorum=false by default; enable for 10% of customers, monitor telemetry, then flip default. Related: ENG-5324, ENG-5488, SUP-1982. Risk: Low; defaults preserve current behavior. Implementation notes: The core changes live in rollout/autoscale/autorollback_engine.go and rollout/probing/aggregator.py. The author intentionally kept the quorum math off the hot path and added a lightweight in-memory ring buffer per rollout to avoid allocations. Merge notes: squash-merged after CI green and e2e passing.
commits: c1a5f9a: introduce quorum-based probe aggregator and ring buffer
d4b2e7c: add warmup stabilization timer and provisional probe handling
f7e9bb1: composite metric matching and decision rule plumbing
a2d3c4b: observability: add per-probe metrics and tracing tags
b9c8d7e: tests: unit, integration, and e2e for probing quorum/stabilization
review_comments: Priya Shah: The stabilization timer default of 30s seems conservative for very short-lived probes; can we make that tunable per-policy?
Author (Carla Nguyen): Reply: Yes, made stabilization_seconds policy-configurable with a default of 30s. Added note in docs about tuning for low-latency workloads.
Ethan Morales: Two nits: prefer context-aware cancellations in aggregator and add a small benchmark for ring buffer allocation overhead.
Author (Carla Nguyen): Reply: Addressed both: aggregator uses the rollout context and added microbench in rollout/probing/benchmarks_test.go; results show <1% CPU overhead under typical load.
Liam O'Connor (approved): Verified the e2e against synthetic variance; logs and metrics show no premature rollback and quorum behavior is observable in dashboard snapshots.
